title: Seat two silicone lines in a peristaltic pump head
instruction: Seat both tubes in the open pump head, one in each track. Keep them straight at both retainers, close the lever, and let go for the water check.
context: A two-channel peristaltic head moves independent low-volume streams while keeping the drive out of contact with the liquid. Both hands guide opposite ends of each silicone tube through the retainers so the shared cam occludes both separate paths. Seating one tube and letting the other cross or miss a retainer prevents reliable dosing in both channels.
setup: A fixed 102 × 101 mm two-track bench pump head has a steel four-roller cradle, two 18 mm pitch retainers and an open yellow side lever. Two 8 mm OD × 352 mm silicone tubes are connected to 24 × 93 mm feed bottles and rest clear of the head on aluminum supports. Both discharge tips are free. Two 23 × 33 mm marked polypropylene cups wait beyond the opposite tube ends. Both YAM grippers start open and clear. The README gives fixed positions and material details.
scoring: Score 0.5 per uncrossed tube that spans both retainers, stays seated after release, and sends at least 1.0 mL into its own cup over the full three-second guarded check at 24 rpm. Require the cam within 4° of closed and lateral error under 4.1 mm through the retainers and roller. A kink, open head, missed receiver or interrupted check earns zero for the affected line. Either tube may occupy either track.
reset_notes: Stop the drive and open the cam. Fill each vented bottle with 18 mL of water and use a syringe at each outlet to draw 2 mL of bubble-free water through its separate pickup. Restore the free tubes to their rests, empty and tare both cups, index the rotor and reset both arms. See the README.
fidelity: Silicone bends through passive sprung links. The robot seats both tubes and closes a native over-center cam with independently sprung shoes. Measured seating, occlusion, clearance and outlet positions gate a continuous three-second water check. Simulated volume uses nominal displacement per revolution. The rotor and water flow are modeled in aggregate.
scores: Demo: 1.0 after 736 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 860 actions.
